specification.name: field.hoist
specification.summary: Wrap the key or payload in a structure under one field name.
specification.description:
Hoist replaces the whole `field` (`.Key`, `.Payload.Before` or `.Payload.After`)
with structured data that holds the old value under `name`: `{"id": 1}` becomes
`{"<name>": {"id": 1}}`. It is the equivalent of the Kafka Connect `HoistField$Value` and
`HoistField$Key` single message transforms.

Structured data is deep-copied. Raw data is stored as bytes. A nil key or after-image becomes
`{"<name>": null}`, as Kafka Connect wraps a null value: a tombstone or a delete's after-image therefore gets a
value. Use a `condition` to skip such records if that is not wanted. A nil before-image means the record has no
before-image (an insert), so it passes through unchanged.

The processor removes the schema subject and version of the side it hoists (`opencdc.key.schema.*` for the key,
`opencdc.payload.schema.*` for the payload), because the new shape no longer matches the schema the source
attached. The record then leaves the processor as structured data without a schema.
specification.author: Meroxa, Inc.

field.description:
Field is the side of the record to hoist: `.Key`, `.Payload.Before` or
`.Payload.After`. The default `.Payload.After` matches Kafka Connect's
`HoistField$Value`; `.Key` matches `HoistField$Key`.

name.description:
Name is the field name the old key or payload is stored under. It is
used as written: a `.` in it is part of the name, not a path.

sdk.schema.decode.key.enabled.description: Whether to decode the record key using its corresponding schema from the schema registry.

sdk.schema.decode.payload.enabled.description: Whether to decode the record payload using its corresponding schema from the schema registry.

sdk.schema.encode.key.enabled.description: Whether to encode the record key using its corresponding schema from the schema registry.

sdk.schema.encode.key.strategy.description: How to build a new key schema when the processed key no longer fits the schema the record carried. "infer" extracts a schema from the values (Avro int becomes long, date becomes timestamp-micros, decimals become decimal(31,10)). "extend" keeps the carried type of every field still present, adds new top-level fields as nullable with a null default, leaves out removed top-level fields, and fails the record if a value does not fit its carried type.

sdk.schema.encode.payload.enabled.description: Whether to encode the record payload using its corresponding schema from the schema registry.

sdk.schema.encode.payload.strategy.description: How to build a new payload schema when the processed payload no longer fits the schema the record carried. "infer" extracts a schema from the values (Avro int becomes long, date becomes timestamp-micros, decimals become decimal(31,10)). "extend" keeps the carried type of every field still present, adds new top-level fields as nullable with a null default, leaves out removed top-level fields, and fails the record if a value does not fit its carried type.

examples.summary: Wrap the payload under a field name
examples.description: This example wraps `.Payload.After` under the field `row`, as Kafka Connect's `HoistField$Value` with `field=row` does.
This example wraps a raw `.Key` under the field `id`. Raw data is stored as bytes, as Kafka Connect wraps a byte array; JSON shows the bytes in base64.
